target.name: Barnard's Star
target.summary_plain: A small, cool red dwarf only 6 light-years away, the closest single star to the Sun. It crosses our sky faster than any other star: about 10 arcseconds a year, enough to travel the width of the full Moon in under two centuries.

render.note: One asinh stretch per detector (0.5-99.7 percentiles of all its epochs), shared by every epoch, so brightness changes between frames are real. Co-adds: IMAGE minus ZODI, official photometry mask 0x3C028E44 rejected, OVERFLOW kept and flagged, then an inverse-variance mean after 3-sigma clipping (drops single-exposure streaks). Then vs Now: each image stretched by its own 0.5-99.7 percentiles. Differences: S/N, linear between the limits.

motion.method: Per-exposure ePSF position fits (D5+D6, S/N >= 10, 100 mas floor); sigma-clipped linear fit with parallax removed
motion.verdict_text: SPHEREx measures 10.55 ± 0.12″ per year toward PA 349°; Gaia DR3 predicts 10.41″ per year toward PA 356°: the speed agrees within 1.3%. Between Aug 2025 and Aug 2026 it moved 10.4″, as predicted to within 0.4%. The direction is 6° off because the saturated core biases the east-west positions (the north-south motion agrees closely).

notes: Each point is one exposure: forced photometry at the catalogue position (ePSF fit, or a fit to the PSF wings when the core is saturated).
Saturated points are shown hollow and excluded from fits.
357 of 358 points are saturated (OVERFLOW in the core).
The quick-look curve is the Year-1 spectral cube at 12.9″ pixels: it blends close neighbours, and channels where the star saturates are left empty.

checks.name: D5/D6 proper motion total within 5% of catalog
blink/difference: first-to-last full-epoch shift is ~10 arcsec/yr northward
saturated core masked in co-adds and flagged
checks.value: 357 of 358 exposures saturated; core masked or flagged in 24 of 24 Phase 1 co-adds

warnings: Saturated (OVERFLOW) in 357 of 358 exposures. Saturated pixels are kept in the images and outlined in the flags overlay; their brightness comes from fits to the PSF wings.
The saturated core biases the east-west positions: the measured direction is 6° west of Gaia's while the speed agrees.
Barnard's Star is the control star: epoch-to-epoch changes of up to 0.6 mag in the saturated photometry are systematics, not variability.
3 of 6 epochs are partial (fewer than 12 images per detector): shown greyed out.
False colour exists for 3 of 6 epochs: it needs D1, D3 and D6 in the same epoch.
